summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA 2008)** — kinship-care incentives  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — reimbursement for approved kin placements

California - Welfare & Institutions Code § 300 et seq. (Juvenile dependency proceedings)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that where relatives requested placement at the outset and the agency never conducted the assessment section 361.3 requires, the juvenile court erred by applying the caregiver adoption preference instead of the relative placement preference on the relatives' section 388 petition.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that an agency's failure to timely assess a requesting relative under section 361.3 cannot be cured by later invoking the caregiver preference.
key_cases.quote: We accept the Agency's concession the juvenile court erred when it applied the caregiver adoption preference at the section 388 hearing.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the Equal Protection Clause forbids a court from removing a child from a parent's custody because of the racial composition of the parent's household, even where private biases might expose the child to social stigma.
key_cases.relevance: Forbids using the race of a relative caregiver or the racial composition of a household as a placement criterion.
key_cases.quote: Classifying persons according to their race is more likely to reflect racial prejudice than legitimate public concerns; the race, not the person, dictates the category.

state_agency.name: California Department of Social Services

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: Detention hearing no later than the next judicial day after the dependency petition is filed; petition due within 48 hours of custody, excluding nonjudicial days
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Child must be released from custody (Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code §§ 313, 315)
